rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 and 3 - authors report their own governance evaluation with the WATERMED tool and a 43-question questionnaire answered by 71 workshop participants in three pilot areas. Q2: Section 2.1 and Figs 3-4 - the platform integrates IoT sensors, satellite imagery, piezometers, open data and delivers services to farmers, irrigation communities and administrations; Section 3.2 - participants in the three areas report that interacting with the platform tool helped them learn about water governance and they intend to use it (94% T<U+00FC>rkiye, 75% Spain, 83% Algeria), i.e. the study's own evidence that such a platform was implemented and welcomed. Q5: Sections 3.1.1-3.1.3 and 3.2.1-3.2.3 - results reported separately for Konya (T<U+00FC>rkiye), J<U+00FA>car-Vinalop<U+00F3> (Spain) and Upper Cheliff (Algeria). Q6: Sections 2.2 and 3.1, Figs 9-11 - platform tested and governance evaluated at the basin/pilot-area scale with irrigation communities and administrations, not a single field. Q7: Abstract and Sections 3.1.1-3.1.3, 3.2 - authors state from their results that end users require technical and financial support, training and time (67-73% say they need technical help), and that investment costs and funding restrictions must be considered.
rows.notes: The study is a platform description plus a stakeholder perception survey and a self-assessed governance score. The perception results concern mainly the water governance evaluation tool and the platform in general, not satellite-based services specifically, so support for the remote-sensing element of the passage is indirect. 'Social cohesion' is only loosely represented (stakeholder engagement, learning, willingness to use). Q3: both sources (governance self-evaluation and perception questionnaire) are stakeholder-reported, not independent methods. Q8: the authors say the platform is not a cure-all and the governance percentage is not relevant for evaluating SES, but do not state limitations of the sample, duration or survey method as such. Q9: only percentages of respondents are reported, no dispersion.

notes: Full text appears complete. Supplementary information (questionnaire details) not provided.
